operation_tail.detail: Ofcom states that Connected Nations is currently published twice yearly, with a main report near year-end and an interim spring update; vintages remain separate.
Fixed coverage, fixed performance and mobile coverage are separate download families and are not merged into one schema.
The fixed coverage download reports maximum available speeds and accompanies each Connected Nations publication; it is availability rather than active-line performance.
Fixed performance covers active customer connection speeds and local-authority full-fibre take-up and is published with the annual main report.
Ofcom confirms that the absence of a fixed-performance postcode file from July 2024 is intentional after the collection-method revision.
Ofcom considers the revised performance analysis robust for overall averages down to local-authority level, but not for postcode-level publication.
The July 2024 collection redesign supports more communications providers while potentially reducing the detail received from each provider.
Superfast availability is defined using a 30 Mbit/s download threshold and is not confused with the decent-broadband or gigabit thresholds.
Gigabit-capable networks are those capable of delivering 1 Gbit/s download; the label is not assigned from lower speed bands.
Decent broadband requires at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload; both conditions are retained.
Ofcom includes premises unmatched to provider records in reporting on lack of decent broadband, so unmatched is not silently dropped.
Fixed coverage reporting normally focuses on residential premises and identifies residential-commercial distinctions explicitly where appropriate.
SME coverage analysis links the Connected Nations premise base to the Dun and Bradstreet Business Universe rather than inferring business class from postcode.
The business-classification source contains more than 3.9 million records across multiple business classes; this source total is not a coverage-candidate total.
The business dataset carries Dun and Bradstreet, Crown copyright licence 10002057 and CACI attribution requirements.
Nearly 3.3 million business records, 84%, were linked through building or street and postcode identification to obtain UPRNs.
A further 550,000 business records, 14%, matched only to postcodes and are not elevated to exact property identity.
Just under 100,000 business records, 2.5%, could not be matched and remain unavailable rather than inferred.
Ofcom removed business records where building/street/postcode matching was not considered confident.
The final SME analysis was constrained to 2.5 million records within the Connected Nations premise base.
SME categories use employee count at the specific site, not enterprise-wide headcount or postcode population.
Micro businesses are sole traders or sites with fewer than 10 employees.
Small businesses are sites with 10 to fewer than 50 employees.
Medium businesses are sites with 50 to fewer than 250 employees.
Dedicated leased-line connectivity available to many businesses is outside the fixed broadband coverage dataset.
Average monthly data usage is derived from traffic aggregated at an Optical Line Terminal or headend, not from parcel-level measurements.
Uploaded and downloaded traffic volumes are combined with connected-line counts for each OLT or headend to calculate average usage per connection.
Data usage was collected per line before 2024, so earlier monthly averages are not directly comparable with the later aggregated method.
Nation and local-authority usage estimates follow the location of the OLT or headend and are not interpreted as usage at each customer premise.
MNO fixed wireless access uses mobile-network capacity shared with mobile users; it is distinguished from dedicated WISP networks.
WISP fixed wireless access uses a dedicated wireless network and remains a separate delivery model from MNO FWA.
CN2025 FWA coverage uses provider network modelling as of July 2025 and is not represented as an observed speed test.
MNO and WISP FWA submissions are matched against the same Connected Nations premise base used for fixed coverage.
CN2025 satellite analysis is limited to one provider offering Low Earth Orbit broadband directly to consumers.
Although LEO constellations can reach all parts of the UK, Ofcom's analysis focuses on service take-up and geographic distribution rather than assigning universal premise availability.
Satellite customer-equipment coordinates are mapped to the nearest UPRN; nearest-neighbour linkage is not treated as exact property identity.
Spring 2026 distinguishes 39,000 premises unable to access decent fixed-line or FWA service from about 4,000 without affordable decent broadband after satellite pricing.
Lower-priced satellite plans change the affordability estimate but do not rewrite fixed-line or FWA coverage status.
About 7,000 commercial premises potentially relevant to USO affordability were excluded from the eligible estimate because some may already use connectivity such as leased lines.
The 2026 planned-deployment report is forward-looking to the end of 2028 and is kept separate from the January 2026 current-coverage snapshot.
Ofcom classifies plans as High Confidence only when low-level design is complete and funding has been committed.
Operator plans may be privately funded or supported through public intervention; funding source does not convert them into current coverage.
The planned-deployment report excludes separate aspirations or plans of national and local public authorities unless represented in operator submissions.
Fresh canonical evidence remains terminal PUBLISHED with an expired lease, no active or long PENDING task, and no second runner or duplicate task.

Forty-five official publication, performance, business, data-usage, FWA, satellite and planned-deployment controls were published line by line; exact coverage candidates remain unchanged pending strict r2 bytes.
